rows.evidence: Q1: Sections 2.2, 2.6 and 3 <U+2013> the authors train and test SVM, ANN and RVM models on their own six-year lysimeter dataset (pepper and watermelon under drip and sub-irrigation with plastic mulch) and report Kc/ETc prediction statistics (Tables 3-6, Figs 3-11).
rows.notes: The study is a primary modelling study, but its own result concerns the accuracy of machine-learning (SVM) prediction of crop coefficients and crop ET relative to lysimeter measurements and FAO-56 values (e.g. 11.2% ETc error for pepper vs 35.3% with FAO-56; r2 0.71 and 0.82 for Kc). It does not implement or test irrigation scheduling, nor does it measure any change in irrigation efficiency, applied water or water savings. The statement that the SVM model 'could help in water conservation by improving irrigation management (scheduling)' (Introduction, Conclusions) is a projected use, not a reported result. The farm-scale (112 ha) calculation only compares ETc estimation error with measured surface flow, not irrigation performance. Hence the study supports only a precondition (better ETc/Kc estimates) of the claimed effect (enhanced irrigation efficiency via ML-based scheduling).

notes: Full text appears complete. The study is about ML-based Kc/ETc prediction, not about scheduling applications or measured irrigation efficiency gains.
